[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: what the user typed, such as 34, already is a number, so a command-line argument can be used in arithmetic or simply cast. Java rule: command-line arguments are Strings; a String is converted to a number only by a parse method such as Integer.parseInt(args[0]) (parse = read and translate).
[1] misconception (M) -> CastParsesString: wrong rule: (int) args[0] converts the text "34" into the number 34. Right rule: A String argument that represents a number must be converted with a method such as Integer.parseInt; a cast from String to int does not compile.
[2] misconception (M) -> ParseAnyString: wrong rule: Integer.parseInt works on any text, e.g. "five" or "12.2". Right rule: Integer.parseInt throws a NumberFormatException at run time when the string is not an integer written in digits.
[3] inconsistent_trace (T) -> CastParsesString: Points to LT (the method reads the whole string; it returns a number only if every character fits the format, otherwise it throws). Applied unevenly: the student parses "12" correctly but expects "12.2" to give 12 or "five" to give 5 on another call. (here mixing in: "(int) args[0] converts the text "34" into the number 34")
[4] misconception (M) -> ArgsAreNumbers: wrong rule: Command-line args arrive already typed, so no parsing is needed. Right rule: args[0] is always a String, so Integer.parseInt(args[0]) is needed to get its number.

[0] names_the_element (N): Parsing is explicit type conversion from text: a library method such as Integer.parseInt or Double.parseDouble reads a String and translates it into a value of a primitive type.
[1] states_the_rule (S): int Integer.parseInt(String s), double Double.parseDouble(String s) and long Long.parseLong(String s) convert s to an int, double or long; if s is not a valid representation they throw NumberFormatException.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The argument expression (e.g. args[0]) is evaluated to a String, the method scans its characters and either returns the number or throws; then the value is used, typically assigned to a typed variable.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Integer.parseInt("123") is the int 123 (same as typing the literal 123); Double.parseDouble("-3.0") is the double -3.0; Integer.parseInt("12.2") or ("five") produces no value but a NumberFormatException.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): The String is left unchanged; the only state change is the assignment of the result, e.g. int N = Integer.parseInt(args[0]); sets N.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Because args[k] is always a String, a numeric argument must be passed through a parse method before it can be used in arithmetic or comparisons.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): SW classifies parse methods as explicit type conversion: a method takes an argument of one type and produces a result of another.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Input-conversion plan: at the top of main, parse each command-line argument once into a typed variable (Sajaniemi role: fixed value) and use that variable afterwards.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> CastParsesString: Changing Integer.parseInt to Double.parseDouble widens the accepted inputs ("2.5") and changes the variable's type to double; changing the input text from "34" to "34.0" or "thirty" turns a working run into a NumberFormatException; converting a number back to a String always succeeds.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use parse methods whenever numbers arrive as text (command-line arguments, tokens of a line); StdIn.readInt() already parses its token; use casts, not parse methods, between numeric types.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The string passed to a parse method must be a valid number of that type. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: Input that is not an integer in digits for parseInt: words ("five"), decimals ("12.2"), empty strings or embedded spaces (NumberFormatException).
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: args[k] exists only if at least k+1 arguments were typed. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: Running the program with too few command-line arguments, so Integer.parseInt(args[0]) fails with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException before parsing.
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A String cannot be cast to a number. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: (int) args[0].
